papers.title: Neurosymbolic Reasoning with Incremental Knowledge for Sample Efficient Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: (Flat) Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents face significant challenges in environments with sparse rewards that require long-horizon reasoning. A compelling approach to improve sample efficiency is to incorporate knowledge into learning and decision-making. In standard Hierarchical RL (HRL), knowledge is encoded in a fixed, non-updatable form, such as architectural choices, and remains unchanged throughout learning. With fixed HRL, reasoning with incremental knowledge learned during exploration is impractical before sufficient environmental knowledge is acquired, leading to poor sample efficiency. In this work, we propose neurosymbolic HRL with {\em Incremental Knowledge (InK)}: symbolic high-level components perform {\em symbolic planning} (e.g. using $D^*$) on an updatable representation of current InK, while low-level goal-conditioned neural modules learn motion primitives through experience using reward shaping. Experiments on navigation tasks demonstrate that incorporating InK substantially improves sample efficiency. Additionally, to perform {\em optimal} symbolic planning given {\em prior} knowledge about the world, we develop Belief World Tree Search. The code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?
papers.abstract: Continually improving agents require dynamic interaction feedback beyond static supervision, yet direct real-environment interaction is costly, slow, unsafe, and hard to parallelize. World modeling offers a natural intermediate proxy that allows agents to query lower-cost, more controllable feedback before committing to real actions. Classical world models instantiate this proxy primarily through future physical-state prediction, a formulation useful yet narrow for agents that require actionable feedback beyond raw state transitions. In this work, we conceptualize Agent-Centric Interactive World Proxies, shifting the fundamental paradigm from physical state transitions to agent-usable information transitions, such as execution outcomes, retrieved experiences or skills, and verification signals, broadening the scope of world modeling to provide versatile feedback for continually improving agents. To systematically map this design space, we organize world proxies into six functional forms based on their feedback modalities: dynamics, spatial, execution, memory/experience, skill, and reward/verification proxies, which together characterize the primary ways world modeling serves agent improvement. We further analyze how these proxies empower agents across three progressive levels: L.1 Inference-Time Guidance, where proxy outputs enrich in-context information for superior decisions; L.2 Training-Time Optimization, where proxy outputs yield rewards, critiques, or synthetic rollouts for policy learning; and L.3 Agent-Proxy Co-Evolution, where real-environment evidence continuously updates both the proxy and the agent for co-evolution. Ultimately, this work recasts world modeling into an agent-centric paradigm, establishing a roadmap for building world proxies that empower agents to plan better, learn faster, and evolve continually.

executive_summary: MIT leads with two strong contributions on safe, time-optimal navigation and motion planning around obstacles, including exact signed-distance CBFs for polytopic robots and a biconvex minimum-time planner.

Multiple works advance trajectory optimization and MPC for complex, uncertain dynamics, from stochastic multiple shooting to GPU-native ADMM-MPC that scales to long horizons and multi-agent scenarios.
Humanoid and whole-body control see notable progress via perceptive locomotion and contact-implicit motion retargeting, pushing toward dynamic, contact-rich behaviors that transfer to real hardware.
Dexterous and bimanual manipulation benefit from new generative and flow-based models for grasping, video-based skill distillation, and human-/world-in-the-loop learning under tight compute budgets.
Navigation and exploration under uncertainty are strengthened by POMDP-based science planning, UAV path planning with social constraints, and robust real-time monitoring of safety specifications.
A growing body of work analyzes and improves Vision-Language(-Action) and world-model-based control stacks, targeting robustness, sample efficiency, and better use of temporal and state information.

institution_matches.title: Control Barrier Functions via Minkowski Operations for Safe Navigation among Polytopes
institution_matches.overview: Introduces a nonsmooth control barrier function framework that computes exact signed distance between polytopic robots and obstacles using Minkowski operations, avoiding conservative spherical/ellipsoidal approximations. The method derives analytical gradients, reveals new local minima from geometry–kinematics coupling, and enables non-conservative, safety-recovering navigation maneuvers in unicycle and translation-only scenarios.

institution_matches.title: Biconvex Optimization for Smooth Minimum-Time Trajectories around Convex Obstacles
institution_matches.overview: Proposes a biconvex minimum-time trajectory optimization scheme that jointly convexifies time and derivative constraints and enforces collision avoidance via time-varying separating planes. Alternating between plane computation and trajectory optimization yields an anytime planner that escapes local minima and converges from simple collision-free initializations, demonstrated on drone navigation and dual-arm bin unloading.

topic_matches.title: CUDA MPC: A GPU-Native Solver for Model Predictive Control
topic_matches.overview: Presents a GPU-native MPC solver that fuses a parallel-in-horizon ADMM algorithm into a single CUDA kernel, keeping all intermediate variables in on-chip memory and synchronizing only neighboring horizon blocks. Across nonlinear robotics benchmarks, it sustains real-time rates with 10–100× longer horizons than CPU solvers and uniquely enables fast, collision-free control for a centralized 10-agent swarm.

topic_matches.title: Stochastic Multiple Shooting Trajectory Optimization via Sequential Local Policy Evaluation
topic_matches.institution: Hopkins University Whiting School of Engineering; Johns Hopkins University
topic_matches.overview: Extends stochastic trajectory optimization by replacing single shooting with multiple short horizon segments linked via local feedback policies, improving sample efficiency and terminal constraint satisfaction. The method also reconstructs approximate Jacobians from rollouts, making it suitable for model-based RL with black-box dynamics, and shows gains on cartpole swingup and a challenging VTOL quadplane landing task.

topic_matches.title: Accelerating Human-Aware Robot Trajectory Generation via Diffusion and Consistency Distillation
topic_matches.overview: Builds a constrained motion-planning pipeline for manipulators in HRI by first generating collision- and self-collision-free joint trajectories with RRT/RRT*, then training a diffusion model to sample constraint-satisfying motions. Consistency distillation compresses iterative diffusion into a fast sampler, yielding up to 150 candidate trajectories in <100 ms with high success rates and reduced joint and end-effector jerk.

topic_matches.title: Light-Loco-Parkour: Versatile Perceptive Whole-Body Locomotion via Multi-Skill Distillation
topic_matches.overview: Introduces an end-to-end perceptive control policy that unifies walking, balancing, climbing, stepping down, and vaulting into a single whole-body humanoid controller conditioned only on depth and velocity commands. By distilling parkour-like object-interacting skills into a locomotion policy and learning autonomous skill transitions, it achieves robust, zero-shot transfer to real indoor and outdoor terrains using only onboard sensing.

topic_matches.title: Shooting for Contact: Contact-Implicit Multiple Shooting for Dynamic Motion Retargeting
topic_matches.institution: California Institute of Technology; School of Computing, DePaul University; Technology Innovation Institute
topic_matches.overview: Proposes a direct-simulation multiple shooting framework that embeds a differentiable physics engine in a nonlinear program to retarget kinematic motions into dynamically feasible, contact-consistent whole-body trajectories. The approach handles friction, impacts, self-collision, and actuation limits without explicit contact schedules, accelerating RL-based motion imitation and enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer of dynamic crawling and jump-turns on a Unitree G1.

topic_matches.title: GraspMeanFlow: SE(3)-Equivariant MeanFlow for Few-Step 6-DoF Grasp Generation
topic_matches.overview: Introduces an SE(3)-equivariant MeanFlow model that learns finite-time average velocity fields, enabling few-step sampling of 6-DoF grasp poses while preserving exact equivariance. On ACRONYM, a single function evaluation matches the distribution quality of iterative SE(3) flows in five steps, and a refined variant improves grasp success by up to 24.3 percentage points in the few-step regime.

topic_matches.title: RoboReact: Agentic Skill Distillation from Generated Egocentric Videos for Generalizable Whole-Body Manipulation
topic_matches.overview: Presents a pipeline that uses generative video models to synthesize human manipulation behaviors, lifts them into 3D keyframes, and retargets them to high-DoF humanoids for whole-body manipulation. Online object-centric re-grounding and VLM-guided refinement adapt imagined skills to real-world geometry and execution errors, yielding robust, generalizable manipulation on physical humanoid platforms without teleoperation data.

topic_matches.title: Bimanual Manipulation Within an 8 GB Budget: Zero-Copy Sensing and Quantized ACT on an Entry-Level Jetson
topic_matches.overview: Demonstrates a practical bimanual manipulation stack running entirely on a Jetson Orin Nano (8 GB) by combining zero-copy camera pipelines with a quantized ACT policy. TensorRT-based FP16 and INT8 variants cut inference latency by 6.4–9× while maintaining task success on deformable pick-and-place, and the study characterizes which ACT components are quantizable under general-purpose INT8 calibration.

topic_matches.title: POMDPs for Autonomous Science Exploration
topic_matches.overview: Introduces the Science Hypothesis Map POMDP, which plans in a belief space over inferred physical properties rather than raw observations, making high-dimensional, science-aware exploration tractable. On extended RockSample and real hyperspectral cuprite data, it improves rewards and information gain over continuous-observation and information-theoretic baselines while reducing per-step computation.

topic_matches.title: Flying over The Uncertain Nature (FORTUNE): Intelligent and Humanistic 3D Path Planning for Low-Altitude Collaboration
topic_matches.overview: Formulates a 3D multi-UAV routing and task assignment problem that jointly handles uncertain, time-varying ground demands and altitude-dependent social and environmental costs such as noise and safety risk. The FORTUNE framework combines offline Transformer-based demand prediction and evolutionary planning with online refinement for emergent points of interest, outperforming prior methods on real and synthetic datasets.
